current_row.boundary_rationale: A dated scene-introduction reopens direct address to the prophet: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.3.6, byte tier) — “Yahweh said to me in the days of Josiah the king” (web:Jer.3.6), asking, “Have you seen that which backsliding Israel has done?” (web:Jer.3.6) — pairing a fresh speech-introduction verb with an explicit reign anchor, distinct from the vayehi devar-YHWH shape used at this book’s earlier word-event onsets. The retrospective on Israel and “her treacherous sister” Judah (web:Jer.3.7-9) closes “but only in pretense” (web:Jer.3.10). The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a fresh statement at Jer.3.11 (oshb:Jer.3.11), marking this unit’s own close.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the 'Yahweh said to me' introductions at web:Jer.3.6 and web:Jer.3.11 as one shared introduction covering both verses' material was considered and rejected: the verb recurs in full rather than carrying over, and the register shifts between the two sites, from past-tense retrospective (3:6-10) to a present comparison and a go-proclaim command (3:11ff).
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: Petuchah breaks bracket this unit at both ends, after Jer.3.5 and after Jer.3.10 (single-witness, tier-3), matching its span exactly. A ketiv/qere note stands at MT 3:7 (single-witness), ותראה וַתֵּ֛רֶא (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier) — the qere is the reading both witnesses carry; this unit's seams do not turn on it. The meshuvah (backsliding) noun that names Israel across this book's wordplay cluster appears twice here, at web:Jer.3.6 and web:Jer.3.8.

findings.defective_text: the qere is the reading both witnesses carry
findings.byte_evidence: MT 3:7 reads וָאֹמַ֗ר אַחֲרֵ֨י עֲשׂוֹתָ֧הּ אֶת כָּל אֵ֛לֶּה אֵלַ֥י תָּשׁ֖וּב וְלֹא שָׁ֑בָה ותראה וַתֵּ֛רֶא בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.7, byte tier), the ketiv ותראה standing beside the qere וַתֵּ֛רֶא with 1 note recorded at that verse. WEB renders 'and her treacherous sister Judah saw it' (web:Jer.3.7), which is compatible with either reading, so which reading the translation follows is not sourceable from the two witnesses.
findings.proposed_cure: Restate to the sourceable fact — the note stands at MT 3:7 and this unit's seams do not turn on it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a comparative statement, then pivots into command: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) — Yahweh said to me, “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah” (web:Jer.3.11), continuing directly into הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier) — “Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Yahweh” (web:Jer.3.12) — a go-and-proclaim imperative carrying the shuv invitation. The address turns from singular to plural already inside this same verse, at לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and again one verse later at וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier). The plural vocative call that follows, שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier), resumes this same plural address rather than opening it afresh, and stays inside this unit on that resumption; the number at all three sites is a single-witness byte reading, the second witness rendering the address number-blind throughout. The promised restoration (shepherds, the ark forgotten, Jerusalem as Yahweh's throne, Judah and Israel reunited: web:Jer.3.15-18) and Yahweh's own reflection on disappointed hope (web:Jer.3.19-20) continue inside the same speech opened at Jer.3.11, with no fresh word-event or messenger-formula onset anywhere inside the span. A narrated scene shift — a voice heard weeping, rather than reported divine speech — opens the next unit at Jer.3.21.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at Jer.3.19 was considered, where the emphatic independent pronoun before a perfect verb, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), marks a pivot in the divine reflection; it was rejected for lacking a word-event formula, koh-amar onset, or imperative of the kind that bounds this book's other seams, so the reflection is kept inside the larger invitation-and-promise unit at reduced confidence rather than split on that pivot alone. A closer rival was also weighed at Jer.3.14, where the plural vocative call שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) resumes rather than opens the plural address begun at Jer.3.12; it was likewise not adopted, since no tier-1 onset of this book's own kind accompanies the resumption.
current_row.literature_type_guess: return invitation with a restoration promise
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A petuchah at Jer.3.10 falls immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); a setumah falls inside the span at Jer.3.17, between the restoration promise's individual clauses, disclosed here as interior texture rather than adopted as a cut given the absence of any formula or imperative there. Two ketiv/qere notes stand at MT 3:19, one of the book's twelve doubled-note verses (single-witness): the ketiv/qere pairs תקראו תִּקְרְאִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) and תשובו תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), each a second-person number alternation. The meshuvah noun recurs twice more here, at web:Jer.3.11 and web:Jer.3.12, continuing the wordplay named in the unit before this one.
